trained_on: real_composite_seg — photorealistic damage + hard negatives on real SOLAQUA backgrounds
epochs: 14 (stopped early; in-distribution val mask mAP50 plateaued ~0.96)

adversarial_finding.interpretation: The adversarial suite CAUGHT A REGRESSION: the seg/v2 model, trained on harder photorealistic damage (seamless-blended, subtler) but only 14 epochs, generalises WORSE to a different DAY than the simpler det v1 (which had 0-1% undamaged FP and flat F1 0.97). At conf 0.7 the seg model reaches 0 FP/frame on different-day but recall falls to 0.45. 'More realistic' did not mean 'more robust' here.
takeaways: det yolo_damage_v1 remains the more robust DETECTOR (0% undamaged FP, F1 0.97 different-day).
yolo_damage_seg_v2 adds MASKS (mask IoU 0.66) but needs more epochs / more diverse damage appearance to match v1's out-of-distribution robustness.
This is honest evidence the evaluation works: it prevents overclaiming that the newer/fancier model is strictly better.

caveat: All on synthetic damage composited on real backgrounds. Not validated on real damage.
